best_for: Home-lab owners with a handful of machines in different places who want them on one private network, for personal use.
description:
ZeroTier One is the client app for ZeroTier, a networking service from ZeroTier, Inc. You run it on each device, and you manage your networks in ZeroTier Central, the company's web console.

Setup takes a few steps. You create a network in Central and copy its 16-character network ID. Then you pick Join New Network from the ZeroTier icon in the system tray or menu bar, or run zerotier-cli join, and paste the ID. Nothing connects until you approve the device in Central, so a stranger with your ID cannot just walk in. Each device then gets its own ZeroTier IP address, and devices talk to each other directly. ZeroTier says a device stays on the network when it moves, for example from Wi-Fi to cellular.

points.title: One virtual LAN, anywhere
points.text: Each device running ZeroTier One joins a virtual network and sees the others as if they shared a switch. That lets you reach a home server from wherever you are.

points.title: Free is personal and small
points.text: The free Personal plan covers 10 devices, one network and one admin, for non-commercial use only. Business use starts at the Essential plan.

points.title: Paid plans
points.text: Essential is listed at USD 18 a month for 10 devices and 10 networks, plus USD 2 per extra device. Scale is USD 179 a month for 100 devices. Charities and schools can get up to 50 percent off. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Not plain open source
points.text: The client is under the Business Source License 1.1, which limits commercial use. Self-hosted controllers are listed only for Enterprise customers.

points.title: Approve the driver on Windows
points.text: The Windows MSI installs machine-wide and adds a network driver, which you must approve during setup. Windows 7 users need the older 1.6.6. The Windows listing keeps 23 versions.

points.title: macOS and Linux
points.text: macOS gets a universal package for macOS 10.13 and later, current release only. Linux is not listed here; ZeroTier's install script adds its apt or yum repository for Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, RHEL and similar.
